choices.text: Hold Capitol Center at the block rate, add a note asking for a refrigerator and confirming the room coffee setup, and set a follow-up to move to Downtown Home2 if the refrigerator cannot be confirmed.
Hold Downtown Home2 instead and release the block now, because it is the only downtown option with both room appliances explicitly listed and also includes breakfast.
Hold Riverfront Courtyard as the downtown value pick, using the bistro and neighboring restaurant to offset the lobby-only coffee wording.
Hold Airport Hampton as the budget backup, accepting the longer rideshares because it has breakfast and the clearest room appliance list.

probes.difficulty_rationale: Hard: Home2 is cheaper and fully equipped, while the block is much more convenient. The key distinction is that the room-appliance issue should trigger confirmation when the otherwise matched hotel is strong.
probes.gold_action: Hold the strong block hotel, but actively confirm the in-room coffee and requested refrigerator before relying on it, with Home2 as the fallback if the refrigerator cannot be confirmed.
probes.label_rationale: Capitol is unusually strong for this trip because meetings and provided breakfasts are in the building. The action still protects the practical room setup by checking the request-only refrigerator instead of either ignoring it or treating it as an automatic disqualifier.
probes.query: Marisol is placing one cancellable hold for a new Hartford arts-funding convening. She lands Wednesday around 7:40 p.m., will not rent a car, and Thursday/Friday sessions plus the provided conference breakfasts are inside the block hotel. The block cutoff is tonight. Finalists: Capitol Center Hotel is $223/night, connected to the sessions, has a restaurant open until 9:30, lists in-room coffee, and says refrigerators are by request with limited availability. Downtown Home2 is $215/night, a 6-minute rideshare or 14-minute walk away, includes breakfast, and its room page lists a coffeemaker and full-size refrigerator. Riverfront Courtyard is $207/night, an 8-minute ride, has a paid bistro and restaurant next door, lists a mini-fridge, and describes coffee in the lobby. Airport Hampton is $189/night with breakfast plus room coffee/fridge, but it is an 18-22 minute rideshare each way. What should the planner do before the cutoff?

choices.text: Lead with Warehouse Boutique for the closer location, higher rating, included valet, and more distinctive room.
Lead with Riverfront Hampton because it has the listed room coffeemaker and mini-fridge, includes breakfast, and still keeps the museum and dinner access workable.
Lead with Downtown Courtyard for the lower downtown rate and on-site bistro, treating lobby coffee as close enough since the mini-fridge is listed.
Lead with Perrysburg Homewood for the lowest rate, breakfast, kitchenette, free parking, and quieter setup, accepting the extra driving.

probes.difficulty_rationale: Medium-hard: Warehouse Boutique is better rated, closer, and more atmospheric, and Homewood is cheaper with a kitchenette. The distinguishing factor is giving the basic in-room conveniences weight without turning unrelated upgrades into substitutes.
probes.gold_action: Make Riverfront Hampton the lead refundable hold and include the listed in-room coffeemaker and mini-fridge in the booking notes.
probes.label_rationale: Riverfront Hampton gives the practical room setup she tends to check, plus breakfast, while keeping dinner and museum access workable. The boutique's style, balcony, and fireplace should not outweigh absent in-room coffee/fridge for this close comparison.
probes.query: Marisol and Daniel are planning a new two-night Toledo glass-museum weekend by car. They expect to reach town Friday evening, have a Saturday 10:15 a.m. museum entry, and want one refundable one-bed room; no dinner reservation is fixed yet. Cancellation terms are similar. Warehouse Boutique is $202/night, 4.6-rated, closest to the museum and dining blocks, valet included, with a stylish king, balcony, and fireplace; the listing says lobby coffee and shows no refrigerator. Riverfront Hampton is $211/night, 4.4-rated, an 8-minute walk or short rideshare to the museum, includes breakfast, and its standard king/queen page lists an in-room coffeemaker and mini-fridge; two casual restaurants are within two blocks. Downtown Courtyard is $198/night, 4.5-rated, has an on-site bistro and paid breakfast, lists a mini-fridge, and describes coffee service only in the lobby. Perrysburg Homewood is $189/night, 4.5-rated, has breakfast and a kitchenette, free parking, and a quiet one-bed room, but adds an 18-minute drive to the museum/dinner area. Which hold should lead?

choices.text: Choose East End Full-Service, then request a refrigerator, because the on-site restaurant and panel access are the strongest current-trip advantages.
Choose Arts District Hampton as the lead hold, and if East End remains a backup, require a refrigerator confirmation before relying on it.
Choose University Courtyard as the value downtown hold; the mini-fridge plus lobby coffee and cafe keep the room details close enough.
Choose Airport Home2 as the cost-saver; the kitchenette makes up for the longer rideshares and thinner dinner access.

probes.difficulty_rationale: Medium-hard: East End has the on-site restaurant and best evening-panel convenience, so the answer is not a simple amenity checklist. The chosen option has to balance practical room details against a competing dining and location advantage.
probes.gold_action: Recommend Arts District Hampton as the lead hold, while treating East End's request-only refrigerator as something to verify before it could replace the lead.
probes.label_rationale: Arts District Hampton is the balanced lead because it directly covers the room coffee/fridge detail while still preserving breakfast and workable dinner access. East End is a real alternative, but its request-only refrigerator should be checked rather than silently accepted.
probes.query: Marisol needs a two-night Rochester, NY community-arts site-visit hotel. She arrives Tuesday evening from Chicago, plans no rental car, and the Wednesday 8:30 host pickup can be arranged from any downtown hotel. All rates are refundable. East End Full-Service is $214/night, 4.5-rated, closest to the evening panel and has an on-site restaurant; breakfast is paid, the room page lists in-room coffee, and refrigerators are request-only/not guaranteed. Arts District Hampton is $209/night, 4.4-rated, a 6-minute rideshare to pickup, includes breakfast, lists a coffeemaker and mini-fridge in the standard one-bed room, and has restaurants two blocks away. University Courtyard is $199/night, 4.4-rated, has a cafe and airport shuttle, lists a mini-fridge, and says coffee is available in the lobby; morning ride is about 10 minutes. Airport Home2 is $192/night, 4.3-rated, has breakfast and a kitchenette, but the morning ride is about 20 minutes and nearby dinner is limited. Which recommendation should go in the travel worksheet?

choices.text: Hold Midtown Suites: it keeps the trip practical with nearby dinner after arrival, while avoiding an upgrade just for a bar or larger downtown scene.
Hold Riverwalk Boutique: the higher rating, rooftop bar, and broad downtown dining district make it the best expression of the dinner-access factor.
Hold Arts Center Block: being attached to the sessions should outweigh the cafe closing and thin nearby evening food.
Hold Airport Hampton: the lower rate and airport shuttle justify leaving dinner to a separate rideshare.

probes.difficulty_rationale: Medium-hard: Riverwalk has the highest rating and most visible dining scene, while the block is attached to meetings. The deciding distinction is simple restaurant access as a soft practical factor, not upscale or downtown dining.
probes.gold_action: Hold Midtown Suites and note the nearby restaurant access as a practical advantage without treating bars, nightlife, or downtown breadth as required.
probes.label_rationale: Midtown is best because it answers the late-arrival, no-car dining need with ordinary nearby options without inflating that into a need for a rooftop bar, wider nightlife, or a fancier district.
probes.query: Marisol is choosing a hotel for a new Reno arts-data workshop. She lands Monday around 7:45 p.m., will skip a rental car, and Tuesday/Wednesday sessions are at the arts center. Each finalist is refundable, includes breakfast, and lists a room coffeemaker plus mini-fridge. Midtown Suites is $205/night, 4.4-rated, a 7-minute rideshare to sessions, with two casual restaurants in the same block and no hotel bar. Riverwalk Boutique is $213/night, 4.6-rated, an 11-minute rideshare, with a rooftop cocktail bar and the widest downtown restaurant district nearby. Arts Center Block is $210/night, 4.3-rated, attached to the sessions, but its cafe closes at 7:30 and nearby evening food is thin. Airport Hampton is $194/night, 4.4-rated, has an airport shuttle, and is about 14 minutes from sessions; dinner would likely require an additional rideshare. What booking summary should be sent?

choices.text: Hold Government Street Hampton: it has enough nearby dinner for an arrival night while keeping the morning pickup and room basics straightforward.
Hold Riverfront Hotel: the higher rating, on-site steakhouse, and cocktail bar should carry the dining comparison even with the longer pickup ride.
Hold Campus Residence Inn: the shortest pickup ride is worth making dinner a rideshare after check-in.
Hold Airport SpringHill: the lower rate and shuttle are the better practical tradeoff, and the lobby market can cover the evening.

probes.difficulty_rationale: Medium-hard: Riverfront is higher-rated and has stronger on-site food, while Campus is closest in the morning. The correct ranking keeps dinner access practical and bounded rather than treating a steakhouse/bar as a reusable requirement.
probes.gold_action: Hold Government Street Hampton and describe dinner access as simple nearby restaurants, not as a need for a specific cuisine, bar, or higher-service property.
probes.label_rationale: Government Street is best because the recurring dinner-access concern is about having a simple reachable meal when she is car-light, not about a specific cuisine, bar, or higher-service property.
probes.query: New Baton Rouge public-art site visit. Marisol arrives Tuesday around 6:50 p.m., does not plan to rent a car, and the Wednesday morning pickup can start from either downtown or campus. The finalists are refundable, include some breakfast, and list in-room coffee and a mini-fridge. Government Street Hampton is $199/night, 4.4-rated, about 8 minutes from pickup, with three simple restaurants within a five-minute walk. Riverfront Hotel is $207/night, 4.6-rated, about 13 minutes from pickup, with an on-site steakhouse and cocktail bar. Campus Residence Inn is $202/night, 4.5-rated, about 4 minutes from pickup, but its cafe closes at 6 and dinner would require a rideshare. Airport SpringHill is $190/night, 4.3-rated, about 15 minutes from pickup, with an airport shuttle and a lobby market but no easy dinner nearby. Which hotel should be the first hold?

choices.text: Recommend Campus Inn because the shortest walk to sessions should trump the lack of nearby Sunday dinner.
Recommend Market District Home2 because it keeps a simple dinner reachable without turning the search into a downtown nightlife or scenic-setting decision.
Recommend Riverside Lodge because the wooded, quieter setting and lower rate make it the better overall stay despite rideshares for dinner.
Recommend Downtown Boutique because the livelier bar district is the strongest way to satisfy the evening-access concern.

probes.difficulty_rationale: Hard: Campus Inn wins on morning convenience, Riverside wins on price/rating/quiet, and Downtown wins on nightlife. The selected answer requires applying restaurant access as a bounded tie-breaker rather than expanding it to scenery or bar districts.
probes.gold_action: Recommend Market District Home2, using nearby restaurant availability as a bounded tie-breaker while not converting it into a preference for nightlife, downtown identity, or wooded scenery.
probes.label_rationale: Market District best translates the evening-access pattern narrowly: reachable restaurants matter, but wooded setting, nightlife, or downtown identity should not be treated as the rule.
probes.query: Marisol is planning a new Eugene community-arts retreat. She arrives Sunday about 8:05 p.m., will not rent a car, and Monday/Tuesday sessions on campus start at 9:00. All options are refundable, have included breakfast, and list in-room coffee plus a mini-fridge. Campus Inn is $203/night, 4.5-rated, a 3-minute walk to sessions, but only a daytime coffee shop is on site and dinner would mean a rideshare. Market District Home2 is $209/night, 4.4-rated, an 8-minute rideshare to campus, with several restaurants within two blocks and no bar-focused positioning. Riverside Lodge is $199/night, 4.6-rated, a quiet wooded river property about 10 minutes from campus, with dinner also requiring a rideshare. Downtown Boutique is $211/night, 4.5-rated, a 13-minute rideshare to campus, with the liveliest bar district nearby. Which option should be recommended?
